APBI 100.title: Soil and the Global Environment
APBI 100.description: Soil as the base of the Earth's ecosystem pyramid. The interconnection between soil, climate change and human activity, the carbon cycle, water resources, food security, food safety, and biofuel production. Strategies for sustaining soil resources.

APBI 200.title: Introduction to Soil Science
APBI 200.description: Physical, chemical and biological properties of soils; soil formation, classification, use and conservation. There are no prerequisites for this course, but background in Biology 12, Chemistry 12, and Physics 12 (or first-year university-level) is strongly advised.

APBI 210.title: Vascular Plants
APBI 210.description: A comparative study of pteridophytes, gymnosperms and angiosperms, integrating form, function, and ecology.
APBI 210.prerequisiteText: One of (a) all of BIOL_V 121, BIOL_V 180 or (b) all of SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 180 or (c) all of BIOL_V 121, BIOL_V 140 or (d) all of SCIE_V 001, BIOL_V 140, or (e) 7 credits of first-year biology

APBI 214.title: Animal Sheltering and Companion Animal Support Services
APBI 214.description: History, philosophy, and current practices of animal shelters and companion animal support services, with a focus on emerging issues from a One Health/One Welfare perspective.

APBI 222.title: Introduction to Horticulture
APBI 222.description: The cultivation of key temperate fruits, vegetables, greenhouse, ornamental and nursery crops in BC, integrated with scientific and practical aspects of their sustainable production and marketing.

APBI 235.title: Biotechnology in Agricultural Food Production
APBI 235.description: Genetics, genomics, and biotechnology concepts with applications to agricultural food production and food safety.

APBI 244.title: Atmospheric Environments
APBI 244.description: Physical principles underlying weather and climates. Thermal, moisture and wind climates from the scale of plants and animals to the globe. Daily weather systems and climate change.

APBI 260.title: Agroecology I: Introduction to principles and techniques
APBI 260.description: Basic ecological approaches for understanding and managing agricultural production and food systems. Includes hands-on field data collection, data analysis and problem-based discussions.

APBI 265.title: Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
APBI 265.description: Principles and practices necessary to understand practical concerns of sustainable food systems. Students who already present credit for APBI_V 260 are not permitted to receive credit for APBI_V 265.

APBI 290.title: Introductory Topics in Applied Biology
APBI 290.description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in applied biology. Topics will vary from year to year.

APBI 301.title: Soil, People and Landscape
APBI 301.description: How environmental factors and landpeople relationships control the distribution of soil types in the landscape and the changes of soil properties in space and time.

APBI 311.title: Comparative Cardiovascular, Respiratory and Osmoregulatory Physiology
APBI 311.description: Cardiovascular, respiratory and osmoregulatory physiology of vertebrates.
APBI 311.prerequisiteText: BIOL 204 and one of BIOL 260, BIOL 361. And 3rd year standing

APBI 312.title: Reproductive Physiology
APBI 312.description: Function and processes involved in reproductive physiology in domesticated animals. This course will focus on physiological mechanisms related to puberty, reproductive cycle, fertilization, embryo development, pregnancy, and parturition.
APBI 312.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 204, BIOL_V 260. 3rd year standing

APBI 313.title: Experimental Analysis of Animal Behaviour
APBI 313.description: Case studies will be used to discover how behavioural principles explain complexity in the behaviour of individual animals and contribute to our understanding of animal welfare.
notes: One of PSYC_V 100, PSYC_V 101 or PSYC_V 102 recommended.

APBI 314.title: Animals and Society
APBI 314.description: Contemporary use of animals for food production, companionship, recreation and science; social and ethical issues concerning human impacts on animals; animals in human culture; protection of animals by society and the law.

prerequisite.raw: At least third-year standing in any faculty

APBI 314.prerequisiteText: At least third-year standing in any faculty

APBI 315.title: Animal Welfare and the Ethics of Animal Use
APBI 315.description: Scientific assessment of animal well-being, ethical concepts applied to animal use, and animal welfare issues arising in agriculture, biomedical research and other areas.

prerequisite.raw: At least third-year standing in any faculty

APBI 315.prerequisiteText: At least third-year standing in any faculty

APBI 316.title: Equine Biology, Health and Welfare
APBI 316.description: Anatomy, physiology, reproduction, nutrition of the horse; common disease pathology, prevention and treatments; equine behaviour.

APBI 317.title: Welfare and Ethics of using Animals in Science
APBI 317.description: Historical and current debate, ethical perspectives, governance, and scientific understanding of experiences of animals in research.

APBI 318.title: Introduction to Plant Breeding
APBI 318.description: Small-scale classical (i.e., non-biotechnological) plant breeding and seed saving. Practical approaches to crop improvement, designing and implementing a simple plant breeding program.

APBI 319.title: Aquaculture and the Environment
APBI 319.description: Interactions between aquaculture and the environment. Current issues, comparison of systems, species, production methods, environments, and socioeconomics.

children.raw: third year standing. Or permission of the instructor

APBI 319.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 230, APBI 260, APBI 265, CONS 330, ENVR 200, ENVR 300. and third year standing. Or permission of the instructor

APBI 322.title: Horticultural Techniques
APBI 322.description: Horticulture theory and methodology in an experiential learning format. Plant identification, seeding, propagation, canopy management, cultivation media, horticultural systems examined in the context of integrated crop management.

APBI 324.title: Introduction to Seed Plant Taxonomy
APBI 324.description: Introduction to seed plant taxonomy emphasizing descriptive morphology and identification. Each student will be required to submit a plant collection.

APBI 326.title: Introductory Plant Pathology
APBI 326.description: Study of the ecology of plant pathogenic organisms; principles of disease development and control.

APBI 327.title: Introduction to Entomology
APBI 327.description: A survey of the structure, classification and biology of insects; ecology and life-histories of insects; insect-plant relations.

APBI 328.title: Invasive Species Ecology and Management
APBI 328.description: Advanced understanding of invasion ecology and the complexities of invasive species management globally in the context of a changing climate.

APBI 342.title: Soil Biology
APBI 342.description: The diversity of soil organisms (bacteria, protozoa, fungi, animals, plants) in natural and managed ecosystems; roles in primary production, nutrient cycling, decomposition and reclamation; interactions between soil organisms; responses to environmental change.

APBI 351.title: Plant Physiology
APBI 351.description: Mechanisms and regulation of functional processes contributing to the assimilation, transport and utilization of water, mineral nutrients and carbon by plants.
APBI 351.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 121 and either(a) CHEM_V 123 or (b) all of CHEM_V 111, CHEM_V 113

APBI 360.title: Agroecology II: Ecology of Agricultural Systems
APBI 360.description: A variety of ecological processes shape agricultural landscapes. Students will learn the research foundations of applied ecology in agriculture and how to read and critique the scientific literature in this field.

APBI 361.title: Key Indicators of Agroecosystem Sustainability
APBI 361.description: A detailed exploration of biophysical, economic, and social ecosystem sustainability indicators for primary production subsystems.

APBI 365.title: Summer Practicum in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
APBI 365.description: Based at the UBC Farm. Application required. Fees will be assessed to meet expenses.
APBI 365.prerequisiteText: One of APBI 260, APBI 265. and third-year standing

APBI 398.title: Research Methods in Applied Biology
APBI 398.description: Research methods including research design, scientific critique, writing proposals and reports, and oral presentation.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in the Applied Biology program or permission of the instructor

APBI 398.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in the Applied Biology program or permission of the instructor

APBI 401.title: Soil Processes
APBI 401.description: Understanding environmental factors influencing soil-forming processes and their ecological implications.

APBI 402.title: Sustainable Soil Management
APBI 402.description: Application of fundamental, unifying, soil science principles in sustainable ecosystem management.

APBI 403.title: Soil Sampling, Analyses and Data Interpretation
APBI 403.description: Field and laboratory analytical techniques in the chemical, biological and physical assessment of soils.

APBI 405.title: Plant-Water Relations for Sustainable Agriculture
APBI 405.description: Plant water requirements for production and survival, physiological stress thresholds, soil-plant-atmosphere interactions, structure-function relationships, cutting-edge and traditional monitoring tools, precision agriculture, application for sustainable water management.

APBI 406.title: Pollination Biology
APBI 406.description: Fundamental research and topics in pollination biology related to various themes in applied biology including: natural selection, insect cognition, conservation and agriculture.

APBI 410.title: Applied Animal Health and Physiology
APBI 410.description: Physiological processes related to common health disorders in production and domesticated animals. The course will incorporate anatomy, physiology, biochemistry and pathology.
APBI 410.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL_V 201, BIOC_V 202 or BIOC_V 203

APBI 411.title: Reproductive Physiology and Technology
APBI 411.description: A comparative overview of reproductive physiology and reproductive technologies in domesticated and laboratory animals.
APBI 411.prerequisiteText: BIOL_V 201. Third year standing or higher

APBI 412.title: Belowground Ecosystems
APBI 412.description: Concepts, methods, and applications of belowground ecology with emphasis on biotic interactions in soil; roles that aboveground and belowground communities play in regulating the structure and function of terrestrial ecosystems and their responses to global change.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth year standing in a Bachelor of Science Program. Permission is required for registration

APBI 412.prerequisiteText: Fourth year standing in a Bachelor of Science Program. Permission is required for registration

APBI 413.title: Stress and Coping in Animals
APBI 413.description: Understanding, assessing, and managing stress in farm, companion, captive wildlife, and research animals: sources of stress; behavioural, emotional, cognitive, and physiological responses; effects on growth, reproduction, health.
notes: APBI 315 and courses in animal physiology and animal behavior recommended.

APBI 414.title: Animals and Global Issues
APBI 414.description: Research seminar integrating diverse information to address global animal issues including: animal-source foods and human health, environmental impact of livestock production, trade in exotic animals.

APBI 415.title: Applied Animal Behaviour
APBI 415.description: Application of principles and research methods of animal behaviour to practical problems in the care of farm, companion, wild and research animals, and in animal training, and human-wildlife conflict.

APBI 416.title: Compassionate Conservation
APBI 416.description: Evaluation of humane treatment of individual animals living in the wild and managed within conservation biology. Assessment of attitudes and viewpoints of the role of animal welfare in conservation biology.
notes: APBI 315 and BIOL 416 or CONS 330 recommended.

APBI 417.title: Production and Postharvest Physiology of Vegetable Crops
APBI 417.description: Morphology, growth and development, production, composition, quality, and postharvest physiology of vegetable crops.

APBI 418.title: Intensive Fish Production
APBI 418.description: Management of fin fish throughout the life cycle; broodstock, egg, larvae, and juvenile. Control of environmental factors, including pathogens, for maximum productivity at all life stages.
APBI 418.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing or higher. One of APBI_V 311, BIOL_V 204 or BIOL_V 260

APBI 419.title: Fish Health
APBI 419.description: Management of fish health in aquaculture; common fish pathogens, epidemiology, prevention, and treatment of diseases.
APBI 419.prerequisiteText: Third year standing or higher. One of APBI 311, BIOL 204 or BIOL 260

APBI 420.title: Fish and Climate Change
APBI 420.description: Effects of climate change on fish physiology, fisheries and aquaculture on regional and global scales. Third-year standing or higher.

APBI 422.title: Indigenous Food Systems in Canada
APBI 422.description: Indigenous food systems are a complex, relational web of connections between land, culture, and spirit. Topics include: major elements of Indigenous food systems and present-day food stories from Indigenous communities across the country.
APBI 422.prerequisiteText: LFS_V 350. Or third-year standing or higher

APBI 423.title: Ecological Restoration
APBI 423.description: Perspectives and practices of ecological restoration in diverse ecosystems worldwide.
APBI 423.prerequisiteText: APBI 200 and one of FRST 201, APBI 260, BIOL 230

APBI 426.title: Plant-Microbe Interactions
APBI 426.description: Biology and physiology of selected plant-microbe relationships. Impacts of plant-microbe relationships on society.
APBI 426.prerequisiteText: BIOL 200 and one of BIOC 202, BIOC 203, BIOL 201, BIOL 233, BIOL 234, BIOL 260

APBI 427.title: Insect Ecology
APBI 427.description: Behavioural, population, and community ecology of insects. Interaction between insects and plants and the application of the principals of insect ecology to biological control of insects and weeds.

APBI 428.title: Integrated Pest Management
APBI 428.description: Development and implementation of multi-disciplinary pest management programs in agricultural crops.

APBI 440.title: Plant Genomics
APBI 440.description: Concepts, principles, and recent discoveries in genome structure and comparative genomics in plants with a focus on economically important plants; applications of genomics approaches to questions in plant genetics, evolution, and ecology.

APBI 442.title: Wine Grape and Berry Biology
APBI 442.description: Grapevine genetics, morphology, and physiology and major biological features of other important berry crops for British Columbia such as blueberry, cranberry, and raspberry.

APBI 443.title: Field Study of Wine Grape Production
APBI 443.description: Lectures, field trips, laboratory sessions focused on major issues related to grape and wine production. Origin of grape varieties and rootstocks, morphological features of the grapevine, training systems, canopy management strategies, berry composition, the impact of terroir on wine quality.

APBI 444.title: Agroforestry
APBI 444.description: Ecological, economic and social benefits of incorporating trees into agricultural landscapes. Lectures and groupwork designing agroforestry systems in temperate and tropical contexts.

APBI 460.title: Agroecology III: Synthesis and Application
APBI 460.description: Application of agroecological knowledge towards the creation of real-world solutions for real-world problems.

APBI 461.title: Applied Agroecology
APBI 461.description: Analysis and solution of problems in agricultural production systems through the integration and application of agroecological knowledge and principles.

APBI 462.title: Conservation Agriculture and Biodiversity Monitoring
APBI 462.description: Biodiversity indicators and basic monitoring methods. Sources of agroecosystem biodiversity, including plants, insects, soil invertebrates, and vertebrates. Proficiency in using techniques to measure key abiotic factors in the field.
APBI 462.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 300, GEOG 374, FRST 231, LFS 252

APBI 463.title: Insects in Agroecosystems
APBI 463.description: Insect ecology and evolutionary biology of pests, predators, pollinators and other insect groups in agroecosystems. Application to biodiversity management and sustainable agricultural practices.
APBI 463.prerequisiteText: One of APBI 327, BIOL 327 and one of BIOL 300, GEOG 374, FRST 231, LFS 252, STAT 200

APBI 465.title: Capstone in Sustainable Agriculture and Food Systems
APBI 465.description: Integrates classroom and applied learning at the UBC Farm with design project.

APBI 475.title: Indigenous Ecologies
APBI 475.description: Application of Indigenous worldviews and knowledges to ecology. Colonial history of modern ecology, foundations and examples of Indigenous ecologies, restoration applying multiple worldviews, and Indigenized, culturally appropriate ecological research and decision-making processes.
APBI 475.prerequisiteText: One of BEST 203, BIOL 230, FRST 201, APBI 260, GEOS 207. Third-year standing

APBI 490.title: Advanced Topics in Applied Biology
APBI 490.description: Analysis and interpretation of current issues in applied biology.

APBI 495.title: Human Wildlife Conflict
APBI 495.description: Evaluation of the impacts of human wildlife conflicts on wildlife populations; application of innovative methods to reduce human wildlife conflicts.
notes: BIOL 230 or FRST 395 and APBI 315 or APBI 416 recommended.

APBI 496.title: Applied Animal Biology Practicum
APBI 496.description: Application of principles and concepts of Applied Animal Biology to experiential learning in the fields of wild, companion, lab, and farm animal welfare and management.

APBI 498.title: Undergraduate Essay
APBI 498.description: Preparation of a comprehensive and analytical review of an approved topic under the supervision of a faculty member. Consultation with a program advisor is required.

APBI 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
APBI 499.description: Design and execution of an experimental/analytical research project leading to the preparation of a thesis.

children.raw: consult before the end of classes in third year

APBI 499.prerequisiteText: Approval of a program advisor; consult before the end of classes in third year
